findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed a member of staff to turn off hand sink with bare hand and no barrier. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper handwashing technique and employee rewashed hands. Ensure staff is properly hand washing to prevent any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed mop to be resting in mop sink. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper mop storage and mop was moved to strainer. Ensure mops are stored in way that prevents any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed no food handlers licenses to be available during inspection. Discussed with PIC, management will take the steps to ensure all food handling staff has the required food handlers license. Ensure all food handling employees has the required food handlers license within 30 days of employment.  

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: Observed PIC to not have proof of sick policy education to staff. SCDPH provided information on symptoms and diagnosis. PLEASE COPY AND SIGN REPORTING AGREEMENTS BY MAY 13. 
Ensure staff is up to date on proper sick policy. 

(O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: Observed store to not have proper Norovirus paperwork. SCDPH provided PIC with information on Norovirus prevention. Ensure Norovirus clean up policy is available in facility. 
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (REPEAT) Ice machine observed to have an accumulation of mold in and around the chute. PIC was instructed to clean ice machine. Ensure ice machine is cleaned regularly to prevent mold accumulation. 
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-702.11: Observed wiping cloth stored on counter used to clean off turkey from meat slicer. Cloth was soiled from previous use and was not stored in a proper sanitizer solution. Ensure that a proper sanitizer bucket is prepared and any potential cloths used for sanitizing are kept inside bucket. These cloths should be used to clean equipment between uses. In addition, meat slicer is in use throughout the day, this slicer should be washed, rinsed, and sanitized every 4 hours. During inspection, CK had conversation with PIC regarding sanitizer bucket creation and PIC opted to using their triple sink in the moment. 
4-702.11: UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning. 
4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: Observed a build up of dirt/mold on the left shelves in walk in cooler. On the wall opposite of this cooler, and magnetic strip is visible with knives hanging. The wall these knives are hanging from had possible drips showing. These areas were brought up to PIC, cleaning will take place. Ensure facility is cleaned regularly to prevent dirt/mold accumulation. 
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: Observed two tiles to be cracked/broken to the left of the table near the front food prep cooler. PIC was shown said tiles. See that wall is made smooth and easily cleanable to ensure wall dust does not enter food. 
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (REPEAT) (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

(REPEAT) Observed no food handler’s licenses for the facility. Multiple employees work for the location, but there are no copies of food handler’s licenses available. Discussed with PIC. Ensure copies of food handler’s licenses are readily available in the public health folder. Ensure staff obtains a food handler’s license within 30 days of employment. License is valid for 3 years. Correct by next routine inspection.
